Course: Anatomy and Physiology for Medical Physics
Synopsis: Human anatomy and physiology relevant to imaging and radiotherapy; organ and tissue structure.
Interaction of radiation with matter, photon interaction, charged particle stopping power, x-ray production.
Cavity theory, ionisation chamber dosimetry, absorbed dose calibration, TLD and radiation detectors.
Cell survival, linear-quadratic model, fractionation, oxygen enhancement and radiosensitivity.
Shielding design, dose limits, ICRP recommendations, licensing and personnel monitoring.
Image formation and image quality; radiography, computed tomography, MRI and ultrasound physics; image reconstruction.
Linear accelerator, external beam dosimetry, treatment planning, brachytherapy, IMRT and VMAT.
Radionuclide production, radiopharmaceuticals, gamma camera, SPECT and PET.
Ethics, professionalism, quality management systems, communication and leadership.
Practical laboratory experiments in dosimetry, imaging quality control and radiotherapy.
Research methodology and dissertation in medical physics.
Machine learning, Python programming and data analysis for medical images.
